Disclosure ruling (#9387, `5323310017`) observed: this record states the rule, the sites and the classes of answer; no probe, context shape, request, posture value set or payload.

### ① Derived judgments

**The one helper — right.** `delegatedOrganizationRefusal` (explain-engine.ts, beside `resolveDelegatorContext`, exported) asks `vetOrganizationClaim` once with exactly the prologue's three inputs: the live organization read off the operation's own context (the same null-and-empty guard the prologue spelled, then stringified the same way), the delegator's OWN membership set read off the resolved delegator context (the set `resolveDelegatorContext` deliberately does not inherit, ADR-0105 D2; the same empty default), and the plugin's posture. It answers the live organization where the claim is dropped and nothing otherwise. Read in core: `vetOrganizationClaim` returns the claim unchanged when no wall is enforced (`postureEnforcesWall` is "not the non-walled posture") and otherwise answers it only when the membership set contains it, so the helper refuses nothing under the non-walled posture, nothing for a context with no active organization, nothing for a member organization. No second spelling of the membership rule was introduced; `vetOrganizationClaim` stays the one, and its remaining import in security-plugin.ts is live (the explain caller's own organization vetting, untouched).

**The prologue (`resolveOperationPrincipals`) — byte-identical in behaviour.** Before: compute the live organization, refuse when the claim is dropped, name that organization in the refusal. After: the helper's answer IS that organization, bound to the same local, so the warn, the `PermissionDeniedError` text and its prescription are produced from the same value at the same point (after the dangling-delegator `missing` throw, before the delegator's sets resolve, inside the same `permissionSets` non-empty AND on-behalf-of guard). The guest refusal, the principal-less refusal and the fail-closed set-resolution catch ahead of it are untouched.

**`computeDelegatedReadFilter` (#25106's arm) — byte-identical in behaviour.** Same point (after the no-set deny sentinel and the dangling-delegator deny sentinel, before the delegator's sets resolve), same warn, same deny sentinel; only the inline spelling was replaced by the helper. The dev's helper-ablation leg (the helper answering nothing, call sites kept) is reported as reddening the prologue's and the read scope's 24 pre-existing cells, which is the reading that proves the re-pointing carries the rule rather than duplicating it.

**Every site the card names asks at the prologue's point — right, nothing left out, none wider than the prologue.** Read at the head, each ask sits immediately after a `resolved` delegator and before any read of the delegator's sets, and each answers the same value the site already answers for a dangling delegator:

- `canReadObject`: after the system bypass, the principal-less refusal and the no-set deny, inside the on-behalf-of branch after `missing` — answers `false`.
- `canWriteObject`: after the caller-class gates, the principal-less refusal, the no-set deny and the unresolved-posture deny, inside the on-behalf-of branch after `missing` — answers `false`; the branch is shared by every write verb the probe serves, not only insert and update, and the organization-wall arm downstream still receives the delegator's sets only when the ask admits.
- `canExport`: after the no-set deny, the unresolved-posture deny and the caller's own export check, inside the on-behalf-of branch after `missing` — answers `false`.
- `resolveProjectionFieldMask`: inside the same `permissionSets` non-empty AND on-behalf-of guard the prologue uses, after `missing`'s empty answer — answers the empty projection; the four public readers (`getReadableFields`, `getMetadataReadableFields`, `getWritableFields`, `getQueryableFields`) all route through it at the head, so all four narrow together.
- `explainOnce` (the delegated path): after a `resolved` settle, before `resolveSets` on the delegator; a refused context leaves the delegator's context and sets unset exactly as `missing` does, a single `delegatorRefused` fold (missing, unresolved, outside-organization) drives the principal layer's `denies`, `crudAllowed` and thence `allowed` (`allowed` is derived from `crudAllowed`, read at the head), and the two layer details name the D10 fail-closed cause instead of the intersection. The agent-only `allowed: true` is unreachable for that shape.
- `describeDelegationNarrowing`: after the system and no-link early returns and after `resolved` — answers the no-narrowing value, as for a dangling delegator (a diagnostic that reports no narrowing for a read the operation refuses is the correct non-answer; it decides nothing).
- `delegatedWriteContexts`: after `resolved` — answers `null`, which both consumers already treat as the refusal (the per-record write gate returns `false` without asking the sharing service; the authored-row probe abstains). Both consumers read at the head.

No site answers wider than the prologue: each ask takes the same context the operation would carry and the same resolved delegator, and sits behind guards at least as strict as the prologue's. No reader resolving a delegator is left out: repo-wide on current `main`, `resolveDelegatorContext` is called from exactly the two files the diff touches (eight call sites in security-plugin.ts, one in explain-engine.ts), the head carries an ask beside every one of the nine, and no other plugin-security source file reads the delegation link at all. The remaining on-behalf-of readers in security-plugin.ts that do not resolve a delegator (the sharing write-scope defaults, the authored-row abstain, the master-detail floor exclusion) answer fail-closed constants or sit behind the prologue (`checkControlledByParentWrite` calls it), so none can serve an admission the operation refuses.

**What stays unchanged — right.** The non-walled posture (the claim stands in core); a context with no active organization (the helper answers nothing before asking core, ADR-0123 D2 keeps those answers); a member organization; a context without the delegation link (every ask is inside an on-behalf-of branch); a dangling delegator (the `missing` arms precede every ask and are untouched); system contexts (the three probes and the narrowing diagnostic return before any delegator is resolved, unchanged; the explanation had no system short-circuit before this change and gains none, a narrowing-only difference for a shape ADR-0090 D10 rule 2 forbids an agent principal to carry). The docblock edits on `resolveDelegatorContext` and the prologue replace the "same organization by construction" assumption with a pointer at the precondition; the inheritance of the live organization into the delegator context is unchanged in code.

**`ExplainEngineDeps.tenancyPosture` (required) — right and wired everywhere.** The one real constructor is the plugin's `explainAccessForCaller`, which passes its own posture (the field every enforcement path reads, set once at init from the tenancy service, else from the org-scoping probe, else the non-walled default); the deps literal is built per call, so it reads the live value. Repo-wide on current `main`, no other package constructs or imports `ExplainEngineDeps` and no package outside plugin-security calls the explain entry points; the seven hand-built test bags each carry the member at their base builder, and the derived bags (`readOnlyRls`, `recDeps`, `recOf`, the `Partial` override) spread a base that has it. The type is exported from the package index, so an embedder is reached by the compiler, as the changeset says. Making it required rather than defaulted is the module's own documented rule for a dep whose omission would misreport (`getPartialMaskRules`); a default would have reintroduced the misreport silently.

**Pins — real negative pins, ablation reported per site.** The 24 new cells in the rule's file run the real engine, driver and plugin with the delegator rebuilt from stored rows. Refusal cells assert the refused value per probe, per walled posture, per object class, and assert the explanation's two layer verdicts and the cause they name; the write-gate cells assert the sharing service's edit gate is never called; the preservation cells assert every admitted class keeps every admission (member organization, undelegated caller, no active organization, the non-walled posture, the narrowing still reported, the gate still asked twice in order); the parity cells equate each probe with the engine operation it describes over a context-by-object table and assert the refused set is exactly the one row class, so neither side is vacuous; the enumeration cell counts asks against resolutions per source file and pins that both files are counted. The fixture's export grant on every set is what keeps the export refusal attributable to this rule alone, as the card's D10-intersection caution requires. Red-first at the base with the new tests (13 red, exactly the non-preservation cells) and one WRAP-mode ablation leg per site (7 legs, each reddening its own cells plus the enumeration cell, plus the helper leg reddening every refusal cell including the pre-existing 24) are reported with restore proofs. Read-only here: I accept those readings as the dev's and note the check-runs on this head as the gate verdicts.

**The moved control — not a relaxation.** `explain-dependency-fault.test.ts`'s "a delegator that resolves leaves the principal layer neutral" runs on a walled stack whose fixture delegator held no membership in the agent's organization; with the rule that is the refused shape, so the control would have measured this rule instead of what it names. The fixture gains the membership row; the assertion is unchanged and its fail-closed sibling is untouched.

**Lane floor.** Every accept-set change in this diff is allow-to-deny, aligned with the operation prologue; no permission or security boundary is relaxed anywhere in the diff or the cited code.
